howToUse: 1. Attach or paste your slides, revision pack, or competition syllabus alongside this JSON file.
2. Instruct the AI: 'Follow _aiPrompt strictly to generate a complete timed Tournament + dedicated customQuiz based on my material.'
3. Upload in Tournament Management -> Upload Tournament JSON (populates the Tournament Editor + Dedicated Quiz Builder).
_aiPrompt.prompt:
You are a Competitive Championship Director and strict JSON generator for Quiz Platform. Using the attached slides, revision pack, or syllabus, create a complete timed Tournament configuration including an embedded competitive 'customQuiz'.

TOURNAMENT & QUESTION QUALITY RULES:
- Write an exciting, clear tournament 'name' and 'description' reflecting the subject and stakes.
- Populate 'customQuiz.questions' with 6-12 crisp, fast-reading competitive questions grounded 100% in the attached material (mix 'multiple-choice', 'code-output', 'text', 'ordering', 'matching').
- Note: In customQuiz questions, use the 'text' property (NOT 'question') for the prompt string.
- Escalate difficulty & points gradually (10 -> 15 -> 20) so ties are cleanly broken by accuracy and speed.
- Keep distractors sharp and realistic; avoid ambiguous wording in timed conditions.

UI & TEXT RENDERING RULES (CRITICAL):
- Question 'text', 'options', 'orderingItems', 'matchingPairs', and 'explanation' support KaTeX ($...$ / $$...$$ with double-escaped \\ backslashes) and plain text ONLY.
- NEVER put Markdown (**bold**, ```, `inline backticks`, ###) in text/options/explanations—place code inside 'codeSnippet'.
- Keep 'orderingItems' in exact correct sequence (concise <= 65 chars). Keep 'matchingPairs' concise.

STRICT JSON OUTPUT:
- Return ONLY valid raw JSON matching the top-level Tournament contract below. Set 'quizMode': 'custom'. Omit '_aiPrompt'.

questions.text: string (required question prompt; $KaTeX$ allowed, NO raw markdown)
questions.options: string[] (4 items for MCQ; optional choices for code-output)
questions.matchingPairs: { left: string, right: string }[] (3-5 pairs for matching)

name: Code Clash Championship: Algorithms & Web Core

customQuiz.title: Code Clash Championship Exam
customQuiz.description: Timed multi-format competitive exam balancing speed with precision.

questions.text: A hash table uses open addressing with a high load factor $\alpha = 0.99$. Which operation suffers most severely when collisions cluster?
options: Worst-case key lookup degrades toward $O(N)$ probing
Array memory address alignment changes to $O(\log N)$
All integer keys convert automatically into floating point
Hash values reverse byte order on every insertion
questions.explanation: When a hash table approaches full capacity, probe chains lengthen dramatically, pushing lookups from $O(1)$ average toward $O(N)$.

questions.text: Predict the exact terminal output when this JavaScript async queue executes:
questions.explanation: Synchronous code runs first (A, D), then the microtask queue drains (Promise then -> C) before the macrotask queue (setTimeout -> B).

questions.text: What Python method removes and returns the last element from a list in $O(1)$ amortized time?
questions.explanation: Calling list.pop() without an index removes and returns the tail element in $O(1)$ time without shifting earlier indices.

questions.text: Order the phases of an HTTP browser request lifecycle from initial URL submission to DOM paint:
orderingItems: 1. DNS lookup resolves domain to IP
questions.explanation: Browsers resolve DNS first, establish transport/TLS security, exchange HTTP payloads, construct DOM + CSSOM, and finally run layout and paint.
